rounds.text: Shivalik Bimetal Controls Ltd demonstrates elite profitability metrics, boasting a Return on Capital Employed of 23.82% against a sector benchmark of 12.63% [E10] and a median return on equity of 26% over 5 years [E27]. The company is supported by exceptional growth momentum, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 30% [E21], a 33% year-over-year sales surge [E66], and a rules-based screen score of 81 out of 100 [E65]. This fundamental strength is amplified by powerful market participation, with the stock sitting at its 52-week high [E50], exhibiting a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E52], and outperforming with a twelve-month price return of 112.2% [E53]. Furthermore, the business operates in a favorable macro environment with the Capital Goods sector in a clear tailwind scoring +1.04 [E75], while maintaining a conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.15x [E38] and a comfortable current ratio of 3.47x [E39]. Conceded: [E46], [E47], [E70], [E72].

The valuation of Shivalik Bimetal Controls Ltd is severely detached from fundamental value, trading at a steep P/E of 62.5x compared to a sector benchmark of just 23.14x [E1, E6]. This aggressive pricing extends to a price-to-book ratio of 13.83x against a sector average of 2.51x, while an EV/EBITDA multiple of 41.02x massively outpaces the sector benchmark of 13.46x [E2, E7, E11]. Intrinsic valuation models underscore this risk, with a discounted cash flow putting value at Rs 749 per share against a market price of Rs 1156, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -54.3% [E46, E47]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the current share price demands an unrealistic 24.0% earnings growth rate, surpassing even the base-case assumption of 18.0% [E48]. Underlying quality metrics show strains as well, with a cash conversion ratio of only 0.57x as profits vastly outpace operating cash flows for Mar 2026, alongside rising borrowings jumping to Rs 71 Cr from Rs 42 Cr [E34, E40]. Institutional participation is retreating, evidenced by negative money flow and a sharp drop in promoter ownership from 51.09% in Sep 2023 to 33.61% in Jun 2026 [E42, E45]. conceded: [E8], [E10], [E14]

conceded: [E1, E2, E6, E7, E11, E46, E47, E48]. While the bear flags these headline multiples and model outputs, they ignore the exceptional compounding machine operating underneath: 10-year profit growth stands at a staggering 40% alongside 18% sales growth [E14, E18], and TTM profit growth accelerates at 30% [E21]. The business generates powerful returns that completely justify a premium, boasting a 26.6% ROCE and 21.8% ROE [E12, E13], comfortably beating sector medians [E8, E10]. On cash generation and balance sheet strength, operating cash flow reached Rs 55 Cr alongside Rs 20 Cr in free cash flow [E35, E36], while debt-to-equity remains exceptionally conservative at 0.15x [E38] with a robust 3.47x current ratio [E39]. Furthermore, domestic institutional investors recognize this premier quality, aggressively expanding their holdings from 1.45% to 14.54% [E44]. Finally, the company operates squarely inside the Capital Goods sector tailwind with a score of +1.04 [E75], proving that market-beating momentum backed by superior efficiency metrics [E8, E9, E10] heavily outweighs backward-looking static multiples.

While the bull highlights long-term compounding [E14, E18, E21], the 3-year sales and profit growth have decelerated sharply to just 7% [E16, E20], suggesting the business is losing the momentum used to justify its premium. Conceded: the company maintains high returns on equity and capital [E12, E13, E60], yet despite the bull's claim of conservative financing [E38, E39] and cash generation [E35, E36], reported profits are not translating efficiently into cash, as evidenced by a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.57x [E34] and a year-over-year increase in borrowings to Rs 71 Cr [E40]. The bull's focus on domestic institutional entry [E44] ignores the more alarming retreat of promoters, whose stake has collapsed from 51.09% to 33.61% [E42, E63, E64], contributing to an overall negative institutional money flow [E45, E71]. Although there is a sector tailwind [E75], the stock's P/E of 61.11x is nearly triple the sector benchmark of 23.14x [E6], and its P/B of 13.47x dwarfs the sector's 2.51x [E7, E11]. Ultimately, recent price growth has outpaced profit growth by 75% [E58], leaving the stock with a negative margin of safety of -54.3% as the current price implies a 24% growth rate that exceeds the 18% base case [E47, E48, E70].

While the bear highlights a 3-year growth dip [E16, E20], the trailing twelve months show a sharp re-acceleration with sales up 19% [E17] and profits up 30% [E21], further validated by a 43% YoY quarterly profit surge [E68]. Conceded: cash conversion is 0.57x [E34] and borrowings rose to Rs 71 Cr [E40], yet this reflects a growth spend phase where CWIP increased 45.8% [E41] while maintaining a conservative 0.15x debt-to-equity ratio [E38] and high liquidity [E39]. The retreat of promoters [E42, E64] is offset by a significant 13.09 percentage point increase in domestic institutional ownership [E44], signaling strong professional conviction. The premium valuation [E6, E7] is earned by operational excellence, as the company’s ROA, ROE, and ROCE are all approximately double the sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10]. Finally, the negative margin of safety [E47] is mitigated by a 100/100 results score [E74] and a strong macro tailwind for the Capital Goods sector [E73, E75].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales are up 19% [E17] and profits are up 30% [E21], but this short-term acceleration fails to justify a P/E multiple of 62.5x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 41.02x against a sector benchmark of 13.46x [E11]. While the capital expenditure and CWIP increase of 45.8% [E41] explain the rise in borrowings to Rs 71 Cr [E40], they do not excuse a cash conversion ratio of just 0.57x where profits far outstrip actual operating cash flows [E34]. The bull points to domestic institutions buying [E44], but overall institutional money flow reads strictly negative with a holding change of -5.15 percentage points [E45], driven by foreign institutions cutting stakes [E43] and promoters slashing holdings from 51.09% to 33.61% [E42]. Superior operating metrics like ROE [E9] are already more than fully priced in when a reverse DCF demonstrates that the current market price demands an unsustainable 24.0% earnings growth rate [E48]. Finally, a strong sector tailwind [E73, E75] and a 100/100 results score [E74] do not erase a -54.3% margin of safety [E47] or a valuation where price growth is running significantly ahead of fundamental profit delivery [E58].
